messages:
maya: heads up, eu-west1 noticed a weird eviction spike for small gpu pods around 03:10 UTC. ~120 evictions in 30m, lots of repeated restarts. anyone else seeing this?
chris: saw alerts too. scheduling latency jumped and autoscaler reacted, then a wave of preemptions. looks like tiny jobs keep getting shuffled between nodes.
leo: quick grep of kube events shows `PodPreempted` + `FailedBinding` for several. PVC late bind delays in front of packing?
anika: hmm are those pods using preferredDuringScheduling affinity to pack onto partial-gpu nodes? that can cause oscillation if nodes briefly look unschedulable.
maya: here's a sample command i used: ```kubectl get events --field-selector involvedObject.kind=Pod -n prod | grep -i evicted``` output had dozens of `preempted by higher priority` and `failed to create pod sandbox` entries.
chris: cluster-autoscaler logs show repeated scale-up/scale-down loop for gpu-pool-eu-west1-small. When scale-up completes, scheduler backfills small pods then qemu-kubelet reports kernel OOM on a node, nodes taint then pods get evicted -> thundering herd.
leo: metrics: GPU utilization still only ~55% but fragmentation score (our custom metric) at 0.78 (bad). meaning many nodes have <25% free contiguous GPU capacity. cost wise we had 12% more hourly infra during the loop.
anika: two immediate mitigation ideas: 1) flip small-pool to `DoNotPreempt` (lower priority) or add `preemptionPolicy: Never` for best-effort inference jobs, 2) increase `pod-eviction-timeout` to avoid instant churn while PV binds.
maya: agree on increasing eviction timeout. also maybe enable `--balance-similar-node-gpus` in scheduler (if that flag exists) to avoid splitting tiny pods across nodes.
chris: we also saw network probes failing for kubelet for ~15s on a subset of nodes (maybe NIC driver update?). that could explain `FailedBinding` transient errors. i can correlate host-level syslogs.
leo: quick patch: set `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` -> `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution`? careful, that reduces packing flexibility. might reduce fragmentation long term if we pin where needed.
anika: can we try a temporary routing: route low-priority jobs to larger-shape instances (1xA100) and keep small-shape instances reserved for latency-sensitive ones? that buys time.
sre-bot: incident created: #INC-2026-439 - eu-west1 gpu eviction surge. Pager assigned: oncall-sre.
maya: i've pushed a kube-scheduler config tweak to bump `eviction-hard` thresholds by +10s and added tolerance for `volume-provisioner` taint for 5m. rolling out to canary (2 nodes) now.
chris: after canary looks good, we should also add short-lived `anti-affinity` for tiny-slot jobs so they don't all target the same half-empty nodes. small change to Helm chart and we can release.
leo: logged followups: - correlate NIC driver update windows - add histogram for PV bind latency to critical dashboard - evaluate packing policy: prefer gaussian-fit over binpack for tiny pods.
anika: long term: consider merging tiny-pool into mixed-pool with aggregator that coalesces fractional GPU slots before scheduling decisions. that's bigger engineering but reduces fragmentation.
maya: thanks all. if canary holds for 40m i'll roll to rest of cluster and update the incident thread. :thumbsup:
chris: standing by to revert if churn returns.
leo: leaving notes in the runbook about `preemptionPolicy` + `eviction timeout` tradeoffs.
anika: FYI cost team pinged, they'll want an estimate of delta before/after. maya can you grab the hourly diff?
maya: yes, grabbing numbers now. will post in incident doc.
sre-bot: update: canary rollout completed at 03:45 UTC, no new eviction spikes on canary nodes.
